evidence: Workbook 'Quality Checks' row 7 (check 6): 'One reasonable reading, and every capability is reachable from the seed, the provided runtime, or the public internet (network is allowed).' The Internal sheet's older 'no network' wording is superseded by the public sheet and the skill's delivery profile (network public); judged against the public wording. REACHABILITY - PASS: environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template (node:22-bookworm-slim, express@5.1.0, better-sqlite3@12.4.1 via NODE_PATH); integration.md is the template text plus the symlink paragraph; seed_data.json holds every record the brief and criteria use (10 users matching instruction.md:19 and app_context.md, 3 jobs with interview_limit, 16 applications with stage/position, APP-301 rejected_from SCREEN plus reason, 127 messages with APP-101 = 120, notes incl. Noor's 'Strong systems answers; weaker on incident follow-up.', 6 read markers, candidate_status_labels, thread_page_size 30). Seed-derived judge facts re-derived: Lena APP-301 has 3 messages, read_count 2, third sent by USR-REC3 -> 1 unread (matches protocol Z); Platform Engineer Applied Greta, Ade, Marco / Screen Priya, Samuel (matches hro_restart); messages are chronological within each conversation so 'counted from its first' is unambiguous. No requirement needs an external service; judge prompts use localhost only (lesson 13). UNAMBIGUITY - mostly PASS: one-stage moves, skip refusal, reject-with-reason, reopen-to-origin, places 1-50 whole number, hiring-manager rights, 401/403/404 statuses, 409 plus who on stale moves with an explicit per-card version (hireops_rules.md:78-81, closing the ABA reading of protocol C), board-order arrival for bulk moves (rules:91-94; re-derived A2,V and Y,W,X), undo-once/most-recent-only (rules:98-103), unread/seen definitions (rules:156-171), drafts per user/browser (rules:175-180), candidate wording table, page size 30. I traced J2 through protocol B steps (1)-(15) and every expected order follows from the public rules. DEFECT - candidate unread count display has a second reasonable reading: tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:346 (hro_unread_counts, weight 2) opens 'Z/U: Lena Fischer starts with 1 unread on her conversation', and prompt.md:33 (protocol Z) tells the judge to 'Sign in as Lena Fischer (candidate) ... and read her unread count on her Product Designer conversation'. The public text never says a candidate sees an unread count: hireops_rules.md:159 says 'We see the unread count for each conversation and one total for ourselves' where 'we' is the recruiting-team voice of the document (rules:3 'the working rules our recruiting team follows'); the candidate section rules:184-186 enumerates what a candidate sees ('a list of their own applications, each with the job title, the team and a status ..., and the conversation for each') with no unread count; instruction.md:7 'Unread counts need to be right for each person' states per-person correctness, not that every role displays one. The golden chose to show a candidate badge (solution/app/public/js/threads.js:221 'candidate || a.thread'), so a golden default is graded without a matching public sentence (REVIEW_POLICY 'No hidden requirements'; Colderwater lesson 1). The seen rules (rules:169-171) explicitly cover candidate-side display, which makes the omission for unread more likely to be read as deliberate. NOTES (no score impact proven, recorded per 'report every ambiguity'): (a) protocol B(12) prompt.md:43 asks Mei to 're-order a different J2 card (Y) within its stage' without bounding the distance; Screen is then Y,W,X,Z,A2, so moving Y past A2 shifts A2's place, and rules:100 'has been moved, re-ordered' plus rules:78 'version that changes whenever the card moves' admit a reading in which A2 counts as re-ordered and the expected-successful undo is refused. Judges will likely move one place (swap with W), so P3. (b) instruction.md:13 asks the builder to run and test the app while instruction.md:17 says 'start with no shipped database'; tests/test.sh:92-109 copies /app including any app.db and does not delete it, so a builder must delete its test DB. This is stated explicitly (single reading), so not a defect; noted as a plausible builder trap. Runtime: no configured judge run, Oracle or model score exists for this frozen input (raw-evidence-index scope says so); the scripted golden results do not include the Lena candidate-unread leg.
counterexample: A conforming app that follows rules:159 literally shows unread counts and a total only in the staff Conversations view and, per rules:184-186, gives candidates their applications list (title, team, candidate wording) and conversations without an unread badge, with server-side unread correct per person. In protocol Z the judge cannot read 'her unread count' for Lena, so hro_unread_counts (weight 2.0, conjunctive) scores 0 even though every staff-side unread leg passes.
suggested_fix: Either add one requester-voice sentence to hireops_rules.md section 7 (e.g. 'Candidates see an unread count on each of their conversations too, so they know when we have replied') and keep the Lena leg, or remove the Lena candidate-count leg from protocol Z and hro_unread_counts; optionally bound B(12) to 'move Y one place'.
